role: Build script: compiled the runner bwx12 on CRB on 2026-11-15 and recorded the build.
purpose: The script compiles `bwx12.c` into the binary `bwx12` with ten fixed compiler flags, tests the binary, and records the build: compiler, flags, checks, the machine code of every kernel, and sha256 values. It ran on CRB on 2026-11-15, and the whole-chip test of 2026-11-17 used the binary that it built.

main_flow.step: Stop with status 3 if the marker file exists. The same check runs again before each run of the new binary.
Restart the script under `taskset`, limited to CPUs 0 to 119.
Set the compiler and the ten compiler flags.
Start `build.txt` with host, time, load averages, logins, compiler version and flags.
Compile `bwx12.c` into `bwx12`. Compiler messages go to `build.txt`. A failed compile ends the script with status 5.
Run `bwx12 --selftest` and save its output in `selftest-bwx12.txt`. A failed self-test ends the script with status 4.
For each kernel that `bwx12 --list` names: append its machine code to `listing.txt`, and write its start, its loop start and the loop start modulo 64 to `offsets.tsv`.
Save the machine code of `timed_sequence` and `timed_sequence_hot` in `seq-listing.txt`, write their branch targets to `build.txt`, and end with status 6 if a target is not allowed.
Write to `build.txt` where five functions start modulo 64, and whether the accepted binaries of bwx8, bwx10 and bwx11 have the same values.
Append the sha256 values of seven files, the load averages and the end time to `build.txt`.
Print `build.txt` and `offsets.tsv` to the standard output.

behavior_notes: The script does not run during the whole-chip test. The saved record is of one run on CRB on 2026-11-15, from 17:12:11 to 17:12:14 UTC [Ref1]. The folder `crb-build-1` beside the script holds the files of that build. The script times nothing and computes no rate.

`set -euo pipefail` (line 30) holds for the whole script. The script ends when a command fails, when it uses a variable that was never set, or when one command of a pipeline fails. A command that `if` tests, or that `||` follows, does not end it. Other failures also do not stop the build. Two examples: a failed `bwx12 --list` in the `for` list of line 62, and a failed `nm` inside `placement` (line 109). The row of line 30 gives the rule.

Records of one build: the binary `bwx12`, `build.txt`, `selftest-bwx12.txt`, `listing.txt`, `offsets.tsv`, `seq-listing.txt`, and the text on the standard output. The rows of lines 38 to 160 explain each record at the line that writes it. The entry [Ref1] says what each of the 24 lines of the CRB `build.txt` holds.

Link from the test to this build: `build.txt` records the sha256 value `cd58e5644cd3e76d58a23569c8a42f4f23e240e5f75cce5f84f6bdf31033546a` for the binary [Ref1]. `go.sh` and `go2.sh` hold this value and pass it to `rx.sh`. All three scripts stop when the `bwx12` file has another value [Ref11] [Ref12]. All 9 `env.txt` files of the bwx12 runs of the test record this value [Ref14].

Link from the build to the local source: the local copies of `bwx12.c`, `bwx12_selftest.c` and `build12.sh` have the sha256 values that `build.txt` records [Ref20]. The binary itself is not under the local folder `crb`.

Compiler and flags against the binaries of 2026-11-13: the same gcc 14.2.0 built bw_old and bw_new with the first seven flags of line 37. bwx12 has three more flags: `-fno-ipa-icf`, `-fno-toplevel-reorder` and `-falign-functions=4` [Ref15] [Ref16].

The branch-target check of lines 76 to 99 covers the trial mode only. The whole-chip test ran the interval mode (`--seq` in the spec files). In that mode the function `worker` of bwx12.c reads the clock and calls the kernels [Ref8] [Ref13]. The build record holds the machine code of the kernels, not of `worker`. Insufficient data: whether gcc inlined the function `call` into `worker`. The output of `objdump -d --disassemble=worker` on the binary would resolve it. The symbol `call` in the placement line of `build.txt` does not resolve it [Ref21].

This script does not compare the kernel code with an accepted build. `check_listing12.py` does that afterwards on the development machine [Ref10]. Its saved output for the CRB build reports 0 failed rows for the 29 kernels of bwx11 and 0 failed rows for the 26 new kernels. Of the six kernels of the whole-chip test, `oldread`, `read`, `asmread`, `read_nop96` and `read_1pl` have the same function text as in the accepted bwx11 build, apart from addresses. `read_nop256` is a new kernel, and its loop has the expected instructions [Ref7].

`build.txt` is written in steps. The sha256 block (lines 154 and 155) and the `load_after` line (line 156) come last. A `build.txt` of this script without the `## sha256:` block belongs to a build that stopped early.

Six environment variables change a run: `BWX_MARKER` (path of the marker file), `BWX_CPUS` (CPU list), `CC` (compiler), and `BWX8_BIN`, `BWX10_BIN`, `BWX11_BIN` (paths of the older binaries). The script also reads `_PINNED` (line 34). It sets this variable itself for the restart under `taskset`. If the variable is already set and not empty at the start, the script does not restart, and it sets no CPU limit.

words.def: the Arm reference server under test. It has 128 CPUs.
the run of this script on CRB on 2026-11-15 that built the binary of the whole-chip test. The folder `crb-build-1` beside the script holds its records, without the binary [Ref1].

the run under review: the read test of 2026-11-17 on CRB. "Whole chip" means: our runs use CPUs 0-119 only: 64 threads on mesh 0 plus 56 threads on mesh 1. Each thread reads its own buffer of 256 MiB from memory.
the two halves of the chip. CPUs 0-63 sit on mesh 0. CPUs 64-127 sit on mesh 1.
one inner loop of the benchmark. In bwx12.c each kernel is a function with the name `k_<name>`. The CRB build of bwx12 has 55 kernels. The operating system kernel is always written "Linux kernel".
the inner loop of the benchmark that reads memory.
portable C code with 16 running sums. Each load is followed by an add. Its name is `read` in the binary bw_old and `oldread` in the runner bwx12.
NEON intrinsics (C functions that map to Arm vector instructions), loads only. Its name is `read` in the binary bw_new and `read` in bwx12.
a hand-written load-only loop. It has the same 8 "ldp q" loads per 256 B as the new read kernel. "ldp q" is the Arm instruction that loads two 16-byte vector registers.
test loops of bwx12: the asmread loop with 96 or 256 no-operation instructions per 256 B, and a loop with one load per 64 B line.
the benchmark and its two binaries of 2026-11-13. bw_old was built from the old source, bw_new from the new source.
later runner programs for the same loops. They print one row per thread. bwx12 is the runner of the 2026-11-15 investigation. bwx11 and bwx are older versions.
two more older versions of the runner. bwx12.c is bwx11.c plus additions, bwx11.c is bwx10.c plus additions, and bwx10.c is bwx8.c plus additions [Ref8].
the build on CRB of an older runner version. It serves as the reference for a new build. For bwx11 it is the build in the folder `crb-build-1` of bwx11 [Ref10].
the machine on which the check scripts run on the files that come back from CRB. It is not CRB [Ref10].
`/tmp/positron-perf.RUNNING`. Another user creates it during a performance test. Our scripts stop when it exists.
the mode `--selftest` of bwx12. It calls every kernel on small buffers and checks the memory afterwards. It prints one row per check and ends with the line `# failures=N` [Ref9].

the two modes of bwx12. Interval mode (option `--seq`): the threads run a sequence of kernels. Each kernel of the sequence gets one timed interval per round (a round is one repeat of the sequence). The whole-chip test uses it. Trial mode (option `--trial`): one pinned thread runs the trials of a plan file. A trial is a series of timed windows. The whole-chip test does not use it [Ref8].

a text file with one line per bwx12 process: a tag, the character `|`, and the arguments of the process. The whole-chip test has three, each with one line: `like.spec`, `cfwd.spec` and `crev.spec` [Ref13].
scripts of the whole-chip test. `go.sh` and `go2.sh` are the drivers. They call `rx.sh`, which starts one bwx12 process per line of a spec file [Ref11] [Ref12].
the function of bwx12.c that each benchmark thread runs in the interval mode. It reads the clock before and after the kernel calls of an interval [Ref8].
the two functions of bwx12.c that time the windows of one trial in the trial mode. `timed_sequence_hot` runs when the option `--hot-copy` is given [Ref8].
a function of bwx12.c for the trial mode. It reads the event counters and the CPU time of the thread at the edge of a window [Ref8].
the function of bwx12.c that runs one kernel on a byte range of the buffer of a thread [Ref8].
the function of bwx12.c that reads the page state of a buffer from the file `/proc/self/smaps` [Ref8].
a macro of bwx12.c that stands before each kernel. It pads the code to a 64-byte boundary and then adds a set number of bytes. So the kernel starts at a planned address modulo 64 [Ref8].
the remainder when the address is divided by 64. It is the offset inside a 64-byte block of code, from 0 to 63 bytes.
the address of the first instruction of the loop of a kernel. The script takes the target of the first backward branch of the function.
the address that a branch or call instruction goes to.
machine code printed as assembler text, one instruction per line with its address.
a tool that prints the machine code of a binary as a listing.
a tool that lists the symbols of a binary (the names of functions and variables) with their addresses.
a Linux tool that starts a program limited to a list of CPUs.
a checksum. Two files with the same sha256 have the same content. The value has 64 hexadecimal digits.
the number of tasks that are runnable or wait for disk input and output, averaged by Linux over the last 1, 5 and 15 minutes (file /proc/loadavg).
Scalable Vector Extension, a vector instruction set extension of Arm CPUs.
`__stack_chk_fail`. Check code that the compiler adds to a function calls it when the guard value on the stack was overwritten.

Lines 4 and 5: no compiler message between them. Line 6: self-test result. Lines 7 and 8: branch targets. Lines 9 to 15: placement lines and comparisons. Lines 16 to 23: sha256 values. Line 24: load and end time.

The machine code of the 55 kernels of the CRB build. The six kernels of the whole-chip test begin at line 1 (`read`), 59 (`asmread`), 133 (`oldread`), 754 (`read_1pl`), 854 (`read_nop96`) and 2126 (`read_nop256`). Lines 161 to 176: the loop of `k_oldread` with 4 `ldp` loads and 8 vector adds. Lines 206 to 234: `k_oldwrite` and `k_oldcopy` with a backward branch each. All six values equal the values on lines 17 to 19 and 21 to 23 of `build.txt`. `find` shows no file with the name `bwx12` under the local folder `crb`.

Test in this task on the development machine with gcc 11.4.0 (x86-64). The C file has 16 lines. Its `static` function `call` has one call, through a `static inline` function, from a function `worker`. Built with `-O3`: `nm` shows no symbol `call`. Built with `-O3 -fno-toplevel-reorder`, and with `-O3 -fno-ipa-icf -fno-toplevel-reorder -falign-functions=4`: `nm` shows the symbol `call`, and the `objdump` text of the binary holds no call of it. The `static inline` function has no symbol in any of the three builds. The CRB compiler (gcc 14.2.0, AArch64) was not tested.

external source: the gcc 14.2.0 manual, chapter "AArch64 Options", entry `-march=name`, read in this task on gcc.gnu.org. The value `native` "causes the compiler to pick the architecture of the host system". GCC uses the architecture name "to determine what kind of instructions it can emit". If `-march` is given without `-mtune` or `-mcpu`, "the code is tuned to perform well across a range of target processors implementing the target architecture".
